quizName:
DMV Practice Test  #8
										  					
  

25 Questions • Passing Score 18

questions.question: It is unlawful to:

options.text: Pass another vehicle in any marked no passing zone.
Pass another vehicle over a railroad crossing.

questions.explanation: It is illegal to pass in no passing zones, on hills, in curves, or where you cannot see far enough ahead. You cannot pass at street crossings, railroad crossings, or where there is a solid yellow line next to your lane. Do not pass when the front vehicle has stopped for a pedestrian or in work zones.

questions.question: You can avoid alcohol-related crash risks by:

options.text: Deciding before you start drinking that you will not drive.
Saying "No thanks, I'm driving" if someone offers you a drink.

questions.explanation: The best way to avoid drinking and driving risks is to decide before you drink that you will not drive. Alcohol affects your judgment, making it harder to make safe choices after you start drinking.

questions.question: This sign is a:
questions.explanation: Warning signs are usually yellow with black markings. They alert you to dangers ahead. These may include a change in traffic direction, a steep hill, or a hazardous situation that requires you to take action.

questions.question: You see a sign that says "Reduced speed, 35 mph." This means:

options.text: The new 35 mph speed limit starts at this sign.
The new 35 mph speed limit starts at the next speed limit sign.
You have plenty of time to slow down before the zone begins.
You should only slow to 35 mph in bad weather.

questions.correctAnswerText: The new 35 mph speed limit starts at this sign.
questions.explanation: A reduced speed sign tells you to slow down. The new speed limit begins right at the sign.

questions.question: You may drink alcohol in a vehicle on a public highway:

options.text: As long as you are not driving.
If you are in the back seat.
If you are in the back of a pickup truck.

questions.explanation: It is illegal to drink or have any open alcohol bottle in a vehicle on any public road. You cannot keep an open alcohol container in the area where the driver or passenger sits.

questions.question: Unless otherwise posted, the maximum speed limit on a public highway is:
questions.explanation: The maximum speed limit on a public highway is 55 miles per hour unless a different speed is posted. Always follow posted speed limit signs.

questions.question: A truck's blind spots are:

options.text: On the left side of the cab.
Both on the left side of the cab and directly behind the truck.

questions.correctAnswerText: Both on the left side of the cab and directly behind the truck.
questions.explanation: Trucks have much larger blind spots than cars. The driver cannot see your car behind the truck. If you are driving behind or beside a truck and cannot see the driver's face in their mirror, the driver cannot see you.

questions.question: Night driving is harder because:

options.text: The speed limit is higher at night.
There are fewer cars on the roads.
It is hard to judge distance and speed in the dark.

questions.correctAnswerText: It is hard to judge distance and speed in the dark.
questions.explanation: Night driving creates special challenges. Low visibility makes it hard to judge how far away other vehicles are and how fast they are moving. You can only see as far as your headlights shine.

questions.question: It is illegal to drive on a sidewalk, except to cross it.
questions.explanation: You cannot drive on a sidewalk except to cross it. When crossing a sidewalk to enter or exit a driveway, alley, or parking lot, you must yield to pedestrians.

questions.question: When can you change lanes while turning?

options.text: When there are multiple turning lanes.

questions.explanation: Stay in your lane while turning. Move from one lane to another as directly as possible without crossing lane lines or blocking traffic. You can change lanes only after you finish turning.

questions.question: What should you do when you see a flashing yellow light?
questions.explanation: A flashing yellow light warns you of danger ahead. Slow down and proceed carefully.

questions.question: What does a flashing red light mean?

options.text: It works the same as a stop sign.
You do not need to stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: It works the same as a stop sign.
questions.explanation: A flashing red light means stop, just like a stop sign. Come to a complete stop, check for traffic and pedestrians, and only go when it is safe.

questions.question: What does this yellow sign mean?

options.text: There is a sharp turn to the right ahead.
You can only turn right on a green arrow.

questions.correctAnswerText: There is a sharp turn to the right ahead.
questions.explanation: Yellow warning signs have a bright yellow-green background. They alert you to upcoming road conditions, including curves and sharp turns.

questions.question: What factors affect how alcohol impacts your body?

options.text: How much food is in your stomach
How much time passes between drinks

questions.explanation: Your blood alcohol level depends on how much you drink, how fast you drink, and your weight. Food in your stomach slows down alcohol absorption but does not stop intoxication if you drink too much.

questions.question: What should you do when an emergency vehicle with flashing lights is near you?

options.text: Speed up to get out of the way.
Stop right away and block their path.
Do everything you can to clear a path for them.
Signal to them when it is safe to pass.

questions.correctAnswerText: Do everything you can to clear a path for them.
questions.explanation: When an emergency vehicle with flashing lights is near, you must clear the way. Pull to the side of the road safely to give them an open path.

questions.question: How can you reduce the risk of hydroplaning?
questions.explanation: Hydroplaning happens when you drive too fast in wet conditions. Slowing down reduces the risk of hydroplaning.

questions.question: What problems do worn or bald tires cause?

options.text: They are more likely to hydroplane.

questions.explanation: Worn or bald tires increase stopping distance and make turning harder. They also increase the risk of hydroplaning.

questions.question: How do you check your blind spot when changing lanes?

options.text: Turn your head and look over your shoulder.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn your head and look over your shoulder.
questions.explanation: Mirrors cannot show everything behind your vehicle. Before changing lanes, look over your shoulder to see the blind spots.

questions.question: When turning, you must ____ your speed.
questions.explanation: When turning, slow down to a safe speed so you stay in your lane, keep control of your vehicle, and can react to surprises.

questions.question: What do construction zone signs look like?

options.text: Square or rectangular with white and red.
Round or octagonal with black and yellow.
Diamond or rectangular with orange and black.

questions.correctAnswerText: Diamond or rectangular with orange and black.
questions.explanation: Work zone signs have an orange background with black letters or symbols. They are placed on the right side of the road, or on both sides if the road is divided.

questions.question: This sign tells a driver that:
questions.explanation: This sign warns that a flagger is ahead. Always follow the flagger's directions. Flaggers wear bright orange, yellow, or yellow-green clothing. They use paddles and red flags to direct traffic through work zones and help workers cross the road.

questions.question: Bad suspension can cause:
questions.explanation: Suspension helps you control your vehicle and gives you a smooth ride. If your vehicle bounces too much after hitting a bump or is hard to control, your suspension parts may need repair.

questions.question: Wearing both your lap belt and shoulder belt increases your protection in an accident.
questions.explanation: If your car has both a lap belt and shoulder belt, wear both. Wearing only one part gives you less protection.

questions.question: To enter a gap in highway traffic:

options.text: Watch only the vehicles behind the gap.
Check behind you, then watch the vehicle ahead.
Speed up and let the other vehicles make way.

questions.correctAnswerText: Check behind you, then watch the vehicle ahead.
questions.explanation: Before you change lanes or enter traffic, make sure no vehicles are in your way. Always check for traffic to the side and behind your vehicle before changing lanes.

questions.question: Hard braking on ice and snow often:

options.text: Locks the front wheels of a vehicle, causing a loss of steering.

questions.correctAnswerText: Locks the front wheels of a vehicle, causing a loss of steering.
questions.explanation: Hard braking on snow and ice can lock the front wheels and make you lose steering control. Slow down before bad weather to avoid hard braking.
